articles.title: French Action Film ‘Red Bird’ Lands CIS Deal as D.C. Romance ‘Step Back, Doors Closing’ Bows at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: A French action film and an American indie romance are both up for grabs with international buyers at the Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market. Cappu Films has sold “Red Bird” to Kinologistika LLC for the CIS region, which covers Russia and other former Soviet states, and has taken on…
body: Shot in Marseille and made independently, the film puts physical action front and center. SOUTHfilms produced it and released it in French cinemas in January.

“‘Red Bird’ brings the energy of its filmmakers and stunt team directly to the screen. We’re pleased to have secured a CIS deal and look forward to introducing the film to more distributors in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.

“Step Back, Doors Closing” is written and directed by Carter Ward, who produced with Jane Hollon and Kathryn Crabtree. Carmen Berkeley and Reilly Walters lead the cast in the story of Ryan and Julisa, a pair of strangers who cross paths on a Washington, D.C. Metro train. Across 24 hours, they roam the city and open up about what they want and what scares them as a romance takes hold. Michelle Macedo, Ashley Romans and Mershad Torabi co-star.
The film bowed at Los Angeles’ Dances With Films in 2024. Freestyle Digital Media has released it in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean, and Cappu is looking for partners in other territories.

articles.summary: Mathis Landwehr-led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS. Fellow Landwehr starrer “The Last Kumite” has also found a South Korean home, sales outfit Cappu Films revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market.
body: Mathis Landwehr -led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS.

Taim M. Adams directed “Lion Fist,” which casts Landwehr as Joe, a fighter who walks out of prison and learns his son needs surgery to survive. To pay for it, Joe signs up for a vicious martial arts competition carrying a $100,000 purse. Gary Daniels, Kurt McKinney, Keith Cooke and Brice Akuesson round out the cast.

Sean David Lowe and Keith W. Strandberg wrote the screenplay, and Mike Möller choreographed the fights. Lowe produced the film with Wayne Graves, and the pair hold the same credit on “The Last Kumite.”
“These deals give the films a wider international audience, and we look forward to meeting buyers for the remaining territories in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.

articles.title: Elke Sommer, prolific German star of A Shot in the Dark and And Then There Were None, dies aged 85
articles.summary: The Berlin-born performer had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman. Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the Pink Panther film A Shot in the Dark, early 70s Agatha Christie adaptation And Then there Were None, and…
body: German-born Sommer, whose best-known film roles were in the 1960s and 70s, was one of the wave of European performers who crossed over to Hollywood and English-language cinema with considerable success, following the postwar emergence of European new wave cinema. Sommer was one of the few German actors to make waves at the time, as Hollywood made much of her bombshell image.

Born Elke Schletz in 1940 in Berlin, the daughter of a Protestant pastor, she was evacuated with her family to Bavaria during the war. Intending to work as an interpreter, she was spotted by celebrated Italian director Vittorio De Sica after winning a beauty contest on a trip to Italy in 1958, and subsequently offered roles in a string of Italian comedy films. She crossed back into more serious work with the West German drama The Death Ship, opposite Horst Buchholz (who would go on to appear in cowboy classic The Magnificent Seven).

articles.title: Margot Robbie ‘May Be Over’ Playing Harley Quinn, but James Gunn Would ‘Bend Over Backwards’ to Include Her in the DCU
articles.summary: As James Gunn’s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Margot Robbie, who played the anti-hero in three DCEU movies, may not be back. On “The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon?
body: As James Gunn ‘s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Margot Robbie, who played the anti-hero in three DCEU movies, may not be back.

“That settles it then. I think that ‘The Suicide Squad’ is within the canon of the DCU. It’s decided,” Gunn said. “I’d say, we have one small asterisk, which is what exactly is the future of Harley Quinn? I want to be given a little leeway with this by the fans because I’m not sure exactly how that’s going to manifest itself. But other than that, I think that we can pretty much say the entire movie is canon. I don’t think there’s a problem.”

Earlier in the podcast, Gunn explained that Robbie has become “kind of the biggest female star in the world” and that he isn’t sure if she’d return to play Harley Quinn. She debuted as the first live-action Harley Quinn in David Ayers’ “Suicide Squad” in 2016, then returned for “Birds of Prey” in 2020 before joining Gunn’s standalone sequel in 2021.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart: Actor who moved effortlessly between Star Trek and Shakespeare
articles.summary: The English actor began his career on stage before finding fame as the captain of the USS Enterprise.
body: Sir Patrick Stewart, who has died at the age of 86, was a stage and screen great who balanced Hollywood stardom with an equally stellar career in classical theatre.
While many actors are typecast, he moved effortlessly from Shakespeare and Dickens to the command of the USS Enterprise and his famous wheelchair in X-Men.
In a career that spanned seven decades, Sir Patrick received multiple awards, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II.
One of the world's most versatile actors, he mastered both comedy and tragedy, science-fiction and historical drama - despite the entertainment industry's traditional dislike of bald heads.

articles.title: I Love Boosters review – supercool outlaw women go shoplifting in Boots Riley’s frantic and funny caper
articles.summary: Demi Moore’s haute-couture maven attracts the attention of a gang of contemporary Robin Hood type clothes robbers in Riley’s fashion biz satire. Here is an entertaining, if very exhausting fantasy-caper about the fashion biz from Boots Riley, a madcap mile-a-minute melee of unadulterated…
body: She plays Christie Smith, a billionaire couture designer who has an office in a trendily designed city block which leans over at an experimental angle. Christie is the object of obsessive attention from “boosters”: supercool young outlaw women who, nettled by her arrogance, shoplift her clothes from upscale stores and sell them on at knockdown Robin Hood prices. They are Corvette (Keke Palmer), Sade (Naomi Ackie) and Mariah (Taylour Paige), the latter having the ability to, by holding her breath, turning herself into a white woman who is less likely to be challenged in a store; an interesting metaphor for what Frantz Fanon might have called black skin, white masks.

For all their savvy, the boosters have a soft spot for certain men in their lives, notably a charismatic community leader called Dr Jack (Don Cheadle), who is running a friendship self-help scheme that is actually a fraudulent pyramid scam. And Corvette is entranced by a laidback charmer and oral sex enthusiast played by LaKeith Stansfield, who turns out to be a demonic male succubus.

articles.title: Ex-Top Gear host Richard Hammond's 'brave' new Welsh life wild swimming and running
articles.summary: The former Top Gear star bought a 19th Century Georgian mansion near Abergavenny in November 2025.
body: Former Top Gear star Richard Hammond says he has swapped vintage cars for food festivals and running as he settles into life in a Welsh market town.
The 56-year-old bought a £2m Georgian mansion in Llanwenarth, near Abergavenny in Monmouthshire, in November 2025 following his divorce from wife Mindy after 23 years.
The presenter previously told BBC Wales he had "never been happier" since moving into the 19th Century home, and each week he has discovered a new reason to be "delighted that I live there".
With Bannau Brycheiniog - Brecon Beacons - in his back garden, Hammond told the High Performance Podcast he had taken up open water swimming as he becomes "braver" than he has ever been.

articles.title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row
articles.summary: The brother of the singer's late personal assistant said she would not have wanted the items to be sold.
body: The guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer.

The guitar was one of more than 30 items auctioned by Sworders from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael's long-time personal assistant. The sale fetched a total of £238,000 excluding buyers' premium.
Bailey died in 2014 and the items were sold by her estranged husband Ian Belcher, who inherited them after her death.

Gerard Bailey, Siobhan's brother, told the BBC she "would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder". Belcher declined to comment.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart Said He’d Never Retire From Acting in Final Interview: “I’ll Always and Forever Be an Actor”
articles.summary: Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles at 86 following “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia,” longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak announced.
body: In his final interview before his death, Patrick Stewart said he never wanted to retire from acting.

Speaking with TV Insider in July to celebrate the 60th anniversary of Star Trek, the actor discussed the projects on his slate, including his narration of Shakespeare’s sonnets for an audiobook and the reprisal of his X-Men role of Prof. Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, which will be his last film.
He added, “I can’t imagine ever officially ‘retiring.’ I’ll always and forever be an actor.”

“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Bush Novak wrote. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
